text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Church and political leaders urge the government to heed demands for minimal constitutional reforms before presidential and parliamentary elections later in the year.
- "Matatu" (minibus) owners in Nairobi threaten to go on strike indefinitely citing insecurity.
- The Ugandan govenment hands over six Kenyans abducted in recent cattle raids between the Turkana of northwestern Kenya and the Karamajong of northeastern Uganda.

- Martin Shikuku, secretary-general of FORD-Asili opposition party, vows to throw his weight behind President Daniel arap Moi "if need be" to stop party leader Kenneth Matiba from winning the presidency in general elections later this year.
- Education Ministry Permanent Secretary Elizabeth Masiga says drug-taking among students in schools has reached alarming levels.
- Assistant Education Minister Agnes Ndetei declares her interest to vie for the presidency in 2002 but dismisses opposition parliament memnber Charity Ngilu's bid this year.
- Opposition member of parliament Oki Ooko Ombaka says the opposition will lose presidential elections because it is split along tribal lines.
- Police in Nairobi launch their first major project -- "community policing" -- to curb the increasing crime rates.
- Uganda plans to issue national identity cards next year.
- Zanzibar invites the International Monetary Fund to review its fiscal policies ahead of the budget in June.
